title: A quasi-finite morphism of affine schemes is an open immersion into an affine scheme finite over the base (Stacks 03GU)
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] such that $X$ and $Y$ are affine and $f$ is quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Then there exist an affine scheme $Z$, an open immersion $j:Y\to Z$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and a finite morphism $\pi:Z\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] with $f=\pi\circ j$. (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03GU, which is Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QB (lemma-quasi-finite-open-integral-closure) reformulated for schemes: for $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}S$ with $R\to S$ of finite type and quasi-finite, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}S''$ for a finite $R$-subalgebra $S''$ of the integral closure of $R$ in $S$.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03GU (lemma-quasi-finite-affine), line 15230, and its proof (Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QB, algebra.tex line 30906)

proof.text: Unpack hf using [pqf-def-quasifinite] to obtain LocallyOfFiniteType f, QuasiCompact f and openness of every singleton {f.asFiber y}. Transfer this openness through the canonical fibre homeomorphism [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. For each x, every singleton of the subspace f^{-1}({x}) is open: write a point as (y, hy), substitute x = f(y), and use fiberHomeo.apply_symm_apply. Thus these subspaces are discrete. Mathlib locallyQuasiFinite_iff_isDiscrete_preimage_singleton gives LocallyQuasiFinite f. This is the predicate-conversion glue, with no additional mathematical hypothesis.

Since X and Y are affine, f is affine, hence separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3); X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply the already Lean-closed finite factorization theorem [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] to f with the local finite type, quasi-compact and Mathlib local quasi-finite instances from step 1. Obtain Z, j and pi with j an open immersion, pi finite and j followed by pi equal to f. This uses the general factorization as a tool below the unit level; none of sk-thm-p1.realized is bypassed.

A finite morphism is affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Since X is affine, Z is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](2), implemented by isAffine_of_isAffineHom pi. Return Z, j, pi and the symmetry of the factorization equality.
